section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study examining how attachment to God moderates the relationship between social comparison and body appreciation in women. The study recruited college students from Christian colleges, with a sample described as young, mostly White, and mostly normal weight. The research confirmed that higher social comparison frequency relates to lower body appreciation, with this effect being moderated by attachment anxiety to God—women who felt unconditionally loved by God showed weaker negative effects of social comparison on body appreciation.

section_summary.extract_value: This is the Discussion section of a single study examining how attachment to God moderates the relationship between social comparison and body appreciation in college women. The study confirmed that higher frequency of social comparison is related to lower body appreciation, and that this relationship is moderated by attachment anxiety and avoidance to God. The authors discuss theoretical implications, limitations (small effect sizes, homogeneous sample of young, mostly White, college-educated women from Christian institutions), and future research directions.
